_note: exp-026 (issue #50 G2, supervisor item A2 / issue #13): the POOL-ONLY fine-tune. Config snapshots copied verbatim from the run directories under the gitignored runs/ tree. Two GPU steps in one experiment id: train_lora.py --arm pool_2000_imbalanced --quantization 4bit (QLoRA on a 4-bit base, exactly as exp-001 trained full_train), then run_decomposer.py with that adapter at --quantization none (fp16 base), --no-few-shot, on the ADR 0007 pinned 600 - exp-008's evaluation in every respect except the explicit --retrieval-input the ADR 0034 amendment requires. Nothing in this file is a measured result.

arm_spec._note: G2 of the issue #50 block (supervisor item A2, issue #13): the pool-only fine-tune. Trains on EXACTLY the pinned size-2000 imbalanced pool artifact the prompting arms of this block retrieve their exemplars from (ADR 0031 item 1; ADR 0034 item 2 pins it here rather than by editing pool_2000, so that arm's definition does not change under anyone). train_source_path is an explicit path RELATIVE TO runs_root (configs/paths.json: runs, so this resolves to runs/pool_sweep/pools/size2000_imbalanced_trial0_poolseed42/pool.jsonl in the repo), and it overrides train_source_key; no cap and no hop filter, so the arm inherits the pool's own imbalanced hop mix rather than re-drawing or re-stratifying it. Measured on the file on 2026-09-20: 2000 rows, 2000 distinct ids, hop split 1461 x 2-hop / 413 x 3-hop / 126 x 4-hop (by id prefix; step count agrees on every row), 0 ids in common with the ADR 0007 pinned 600 (the assertion in src/finetune_data.py runs it again every run), sha256 cc3646625d759a1b58179b18c25f83d255db24f05acc08b666985af2e58d6646 - the same pool hash configs/decomposer_musique.json records for the retrieval artifact of this block. The rows carry no 'question_decomposition', so data.step_fields resolves to 'few_shot_decomposition_musique'. The training run records the resolved path AND that sha256, so a later reader can tell a regenerated pool from this one.

prompt._note: The training prompt is built from the SAME per-model prompt file the prompting arm uses (components/decomposer/models/<model>/), with the few-shot block empty: the fine-tuned arm is meant to answer zero-shot, and inference must see the string shape training saw (run_decomposer.py --adapter ... --no-few-shot). target_reference_style 'as_is' trains on the gold step text verbatim; 'bracketed' rewrites '#1' to '[#1]' to match the convention the prompt file states. The choice is not neutral and is Jahid's to make: the evaluator strips brackets before matching steps (so exact-match and step-F1 are unaffected), but reference_validity_micro is vacuously 1.0 for predictions with no [#k] references, and ROUGE-L tokenises before punctuation stripping, so '#1' and '[#1]' are different tokens there.
prompt._unguided_hop_placeholder_note: Not duplicated here: it is read from decomposer_config below, so the training prompt and the inference prompt cannot drift apart on it.

loader._note: Base-model loading for training. QLoRA is the 4bit path (bitsandbytes NF4 + double quantization); 'none' loads in dtype. device_map 'auto' needs accelerate.

lora._note: target_modules are the attention/MLP projection names of Llama/Mistral-family models. A different base architecture uses different names, so this list is a config value, not a default buried in code; peft raises if a name is absent.

training._note: trl SFTConfig fields. The dataset is prompt/completion typed and completion_only_loss masks the prompt out of the loss, so the model is trained on the decomposition text only. Batch 1 x grad-accum 16 with gradient checkpointing and max_length 1024 is what keeps a 4-bit 7B base inside 24 GiB on the RTX 3090 of docs/compute.md - an estimate until a run measures peak_gpu_memory_bytes, which the metrics JSON records. bf16 is supported on Ampere.
training._warmup_note: warmup_steps, not warmup_ratio: transformers 5.5.4 warns that warmup_ratio is deprecated and slated for removal, so the run would emit a deprecation warning and eventually break.

hop_lines_removed: - The number of steps MUST equal the hop count.

condition_settings._note: No hop count in the prompt: the model decides how many steps to emit.

hop_source.note: the query's gold hop depth (from its id on the retrieval path, or from the per-hop file it was read from) - never a prediction

few_shot_self_exclusion.note: no few-shot examples were selected in this run, so there was nothing to self-exclude

ged_policy.cost_bound: max_nodes_for_optimizer is the guard that bounds cost: it is checked before any search starts and is deterministic. per_item_time_budget_seconds is a backstop only - the deadline is tested between the optimizer's successive approximations, so a single long-running approximation (including the first) cannot be interrupted
ged_policy.on_exhaustion: the item is reported with a documented upper bound and flagged in ged_fallback, never dropped (dropping would break the paired battery; Break's own evaluator drops such items) — ADR 0026
ged_policy.node_substitution_cost: 1 - the edit-distance match ratio over lowercased whitespace tokens; Break lemmatizes with spaCy en_core_web_sm, so absolute values are not comparable to published Break GED
ged_policy.direction: lower is better (it is a distance)
ged_policy.machine_dependence: ged_fallback_counts['time_budget'] is machine-dependent, and so are the values of the items it counts (the last approximation before the deadline); every other path, including 'node_cap' and 'no_optimizer_result', is deterministic. An empty ged_fallback_counts means no machine-dependent value in the run

decomp_mean_policy.formula: per item, the unweighted mean over the components of: break_exact_match, sari, 1 - min(ged_clamp, ged), chain_validity, hop_count_exact_match
decomp_mean_policy.weights: all equal by construction; there is no weighted variant
decomp_mean_policy.status: CONTINGENCY, not part of the reported suite. Offered only against a requirement for one blended number, reported beside the suite and never instead of it
decomp_mean_policy.junk_gate: GATE PASSED on the ADR 0007 pinned 600 (all 15 rows on the same 600 items): the best junk baseline scored decomp_mean 0.1412 (J4, three fixed steps) against a real-arm worst of 0.5085 (exp005 unguided / unguided_capped), a margin of +0.3673, and every one of J1-J4 ranked below every one of the nine committed arms. Re-derive with scripts/decomposition_junk_battery.py; the table is in ADR 0029.
